correctness.rationale: Integrating the interior measure D²f twice gives a hinge integral modulo an affine function. The affine part is reproduced for n≥1. The triangle inequality gives the upper norm bound and a hinge at a maximizing interior knot attains it (the endpoint residuals are zero, whereas each interior residual is nonzero). In equality, pairing the signed residual integral with its own unit direction forces almost every signed residual to be the same maximal vector. Their second distributional derivatives have atoms at their respective knots and otherwise are smooth, so this is possible only for a single knot. For the factorization, write a=t(1−t), J_j=P_j^{(1,1)}(2t−1). The shifted Legendre differential equation gives c_j′=−aJ_{j−1}/j; the weighted Jacobi equation integrated from 1 gives c_j=a²P_{j−2}^{(2,2)}(2t−1)/(j(j−1)) for j≥2. The difference J_{j−2}/(j−1)−J_j/(j+1) vanishes at both endpoints; its quotient by 1−z² is orthogonal with weight (1−z²)² to degrees ≤j−3 and leading coefficients give the stated connection constant. This proves that the difference between successive proposed derivatives equals −2(2j+1)c_jc_j′; the degree-one base is a³/3. Jacobi interlacing supplies exactly 2n−1 simple interior stationary points, and parity and positive leading coefficients give the stated strict midpoint signs. The degree-two maximizing a is 1/5, while the degree-three candidates a=1/7, 1/5, 1/4 give 1/7203, 1/9375, 1/3072, respectively; degree one peaks at a=1/4. These verify both constants and knot sets. The frozen SymPy checker was inspected, not executed; its reported finite identities are not the all-degree proof.

evidence: Theorem 3.4(ii), equation (3.47), is an L² upper estimate under derivative-variation hypotheses, proved using a Legendre Parseval tail and coefficient bounds. It does not give an exact sharp hinge maximum or all stationary points under those hypotheses.

evidence: Taking the order-one hinge in the coefficient representation gives known coefficients after rescaling; Parseval gives an exact unevaluated residual tail. Related sharp-norm records already use reduction to single singularities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the coefficient representation and the general point-mass strategy. The inspected results do not provide that implication as an instance of a stronger sharp theorem.

evidence: The first-order BV record on (−1,1) uses jump functions and stationary derivative −P_nP_{n+1}. Record e5d536b3b33f uses the Bernstein approximation operator on the same curvature class, not orthogonal projection.
Liu–Wang–Wu's interval and Jacobi normalization can be mapped to the frozen interval by x↦2x−1; their coefficient formula then has the same hinge input.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Affine rescaling preserves the type of derivative-variation seminorm; it does not convert first-order variation to second-order variation. Differentiating the orthogonal projection does not give the unweighted Legendre projection of the derivative, so the first-order derivative law does not transfer directly. Replacing the projection by Bernstein approximation likewise changes the residual kernel.

value.rationale: The sharp norm over a natural variation ball is reduced to a finite exact list for every degree, rather than a bound or a search over all knots. The equality rigidity and the first three global cases show why selecting a knot matters; already at degree two, the midpoint is not worst. This is useful independently of any new global classification of the maximizing roots.
